summary.title: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
summary.primary_objective: Consolidates and amends laws regulating the occupational safety, health and working conditions of persons employed in an establishment, covering factories, mines, dock work, and contract labour.
enforcing_spheres: Directorate General Factory Advice Service and Labour Institutes (DGFASLI)
State Directorate of Industrial Safety & Health (DISH)
repealed_acts: The Dock Workers (Safety, Health and Welfare) Act, 1986
The Building and Other Construction Workers Act, 1996
The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970
The Beedi and Cigar Workers Act, 1966
mandatory_registers: Form 18 - Notice of Accident / Dangerous Occurrence

sections.code_name: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
sections.title: Definition of Factory
sections.statutory_text: Factory means any premises where twenty or more workers are working, or were working on any day of the preceding twelve months, and in any part of which a manufacturing process is being carried on with the aid of power; or forty or more workers where manufacturing is carried on without the aid of power.

penalties.subsequent_offense: Imprisonment up to 2 years and fine up to ₹5,00,000

sections.code_name: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
sections.title: Safety Committee and Safety Officers
sections.statutory_text: In every factory wherein two hundred and fifty or more workers are ordinarily employed, or in which hazardous process is carried on wherein one hundred or more workers are employed, the employer shall constitute in the prescribed manner a Safety Committee consisting of equal representatives of employer and workers to promote safety cooperation. Every factory employing 500+ workers must appoint a qualified Safety Officer.

penalties.subsequent_offense: Fine up to ₹3,00,000 or imprisonment up to 6 months

mandatory_registers: Safety Committee Minutes & Action Plan Register

sections.code_name: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
sections.chapter_title: Working Hours and Annual Leave with Wages
sections.title: Daily and Weekly Working Hours and Spread-over
sections.statutory_text: No worker shall be required or allowed to work in any establishment for more than eight hours in any day or for more than forty-eight hours in any week. The periods of work of adult workers shall be so fixed that no period shall exceed five hours before an interval of rest of at least half an hour. Spread-over including rest interval shall not exceed twelve hours in any day.

thresholds.criterion: Daily and weekly working hours ceiling

penalties.subsequent_offense: Fine up to ₹1,00,000 or imprisonment up to 3 months

mandatory_registers: Form D - Muster Roll / Attendance Register

sections.code_name: The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
sections.title: Welfare Facilities (Canteens, Crèches, First Aid)
sections.statutory_text: Every establishment employing one hundred or more workers shall provide and maintain an adequate canteen facility. Every establishment employing fifty or more workers shall provide and maintain a suitable crèche for the use of children under the age of six years. First aid boxes equipped with prescribed contents must be maintained at the rate of one for every fifty workers.

thresholds.criterion: Establishment worker count for welfare facilities
thresholds.applicability_limit: Canteen: 100+ workers | Crèche: 50+ workers | First Aid: 1 per 50 workers
